witness.note: Leges Henrici primi: Liebermann’s edited Latin text, from the manuscripts he names in Gesetze I, p. 547, note a, listed below
London, The National Archives (formerly the Public Record Office), E 164/2 (the Red Book of the Exchequer)
The original of the London collection, Leges Anglorum Londoniis collectae (c. 1210), which survives in copies
London, British Library, Cotton MS Claudius D.ii (Liebermann’s K, also K2)
John Selden’s manuscript, now lost (known from Twysden’s variants)
Roger Twysden, in Wheloc’s edition of Lambarde’s Archaionomia (Cambridge, 1644)
London, Guildhall (Corporation of London), a lost manuscript (there from at least 1639 to 1721), known only from the variants cited by earlier editors as “Lond”
Manchester, John Rylands Library, MS Latin 155

div.head: Hn 55.3b
div.ab: Set fides habeatur dominis omnibus, salua fide precedencium, et magis ei cuius ligius est; et eius licencia sit, si quis eius (aliquem) alium sibi dominum faciat.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 575 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: dem Angelsächsischen Verbot eigenmächtigen Herrensuchens, wie II Cn. 28, das Allen vergleicht, ist fremd das Beibehalten des bisherigen wie der Ligius
the retention of the previous [lord], as with the ligius, is foreign to the Anglo-Saxon prohibition of seeking a lord on one’s own authority, as in II Cn. 28, which Allen compares
hominum ergänzt ohne Hss. Wi Tho. [nicht nöthig]
hominum supplied without MSS Wi Tho. [not necessary]

div.ab: But let faith be kept to all lords, saving the faith owed to the earlier ones, and most to him whose liege man he is; and let it be with his leave, if any man of his makes (any) other his lord.
